parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents no traveler-facing restriction: no criminalisation of expression, no facility or border rule, no police targeting, no trans-specific violence pattern, no custody or care-denial exposure. Gender-marker change is resident-facing litigation, not a visitor rule. Positives are substantive — appellate and constitutional courts rulings for trans recognition, employment protection naming gender identity, hate-speech/discrimination penalties, registering LGBTI organisations, abolished death penalty. Pulling down: enforcement and social conditions explicitly lag the law, with documented daily discrimination, violence and stigmatisation against LGBTI people (undated, not trans-specific); whether hate-crime provisions reach gender identity is unresolved; advocacy exclusion shows consultation gaps. Net: functioning remedies against real but non-universal social friction, no documented state-imposed exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or document friction for trans visitors; no X-marker or mismatch policy stated either way.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of gender expression; entry rules not documented as restricting trans travelers.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks interact only with the visitor's home passport; no local gender-recognition regime is engaged.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention or custody practice targeting trans people; no morality, fraud or presentation statute cited.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Death penalty abolished (penal code 2015, military code 2021); courts demonstrably grant relief to trans litigants.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Absent any documented lever, no interaction chain from routine contact to custody is evidenced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access, ward-placement or strip-search rule documented at any level of government.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No subnational variation recorded; nothing in the record imposes birth-sex placement on visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Subnational picture is explicitly unevidenced — an open question, not an exposure.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial to trans visitors; no HRT import or prescription rule stated.
care_services.protection: Constitutional 'any other status' read by authorities to cover gender identity; employment-sector protection names gender identity.
care_services.interaction: Whether hate-speech/discrimination penalties (SO only expressly) extend to gender identity is unresolved — an open question.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State frames discrimination negatively: 2015 penal provisions punish orientation-based hate speech and service discrimination; constitutional court calls Civil Code outdated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No state threat-framing; monitoring bodies and a labour-market commission exist; LGBTI organisations may register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Implementation lag means protections bind institutions more reliably than they shape street attitudes.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-dependent rule, minor-specific exposure, or family-custody provision documented for traveling guardians.
minors_guardians.protection: Equal age of consent since 2015; no documented child-protection scrutiny of trans guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure would run through ordinary document and accommodation checks, none documented as problematic.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: UN submission records daily discrimination, violence and stigmatisation against LGBTI people; 2015 report notes discrimination. Undated, LGBTI-wide, not trans-specific, no pattern counts or state implication.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented police targeting of trans people; criminal penalties exist for discrimination; civil society documents and litigates openly.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social hostility without state complicity or remedy-failure leaves recourse intact, capping severity at the friction-to-hostility range.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement lags legal position; advocacy coalition excluded from consultation; hate-crime coverage of gender identity unstated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Appellate victory 2022, constitutional criticism 2023, binding regional judgment, employment protection 2022 — courts demonstrably work for trans people.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts partially mediate the enforcement gap; recurring failures are not documented, so remedies reduce rather than fail.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this. Vellandra has a universal, routine, state-imposed entry bar with no remedy — a tier-1 exposure. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no registration, no exclusion of any kind against visitors. Its negatives are undated societal friction plus enforcement lag, a tier-3 feature, far below a border exclusion regime.

Higher than this. Kestrel Isles has documented, recurring border secondary screening and discretionary entry refusal specific to trans travelers — a universal-exposure measure. This dossier records no border friction at all, no administrative detention pathway, and working courts. Its lagging enforcement lacks a documented traveler-facing mechanism, so it sits above the 0.55 tier.

Similar, slightly below. Meridia documents real border secondary screening with training and a functioning tribunal — an exposure with a remedy. Here there is no documented screening exposure at all (a plus), but Meridia's society is described as broadly tolerant while this dossier explicitly records daily discrimination and violence lagging the law, pulling it a step below.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is protective on paper with institutions that demonstrably deliver for trans people (2017/2022 judgments, constitutional criticism of the Civil Code, binding regional ruling, 2025 marriage ruling, 2025 employment protection), no criminalisation, no expression offence, no facility, border, custody or care exposure, and an abolished death penalty. The documented deficit is implementation: discrimination, violence and stigmatisation persist per an undated LGBTI-wide UN submission, gender identity's coverage under hate-speech provisions is unstated, and advocacy voices are excluded from consultation. Because no universal-exposure measure or state-imposed constraint reaches a visitor, and remedies function rather than recur unrepaired, the friction stays in the social tier — placing the score in the upper Reduced Risk range rather than at the low end of it.
